title: Judges 3
paragraphs: ¹ These are the nations the LORD left in the land to test the Israelites — all those who had not experienced any of the wars in Canaan. ² He did this to teach warfare to the descendants of the Israelites who had not previously known battle. ³ He left the five rulers of the Philistines, all the Canaanites, the Sidonians, and the Hivites living in the Lebanon mountains from Mount Baal-hermon to the entrance of Hamath. ⁴ They were left to test Israel — to see whether they would obey the LORD's commands, which he had given their ancestors through Moses. ⁵ The Israelites lived among the Canaanites, Hittites, Amorites, Perizzites, Hivites, and Jebusites.

⁶ They took the daughters of these peoples as wives and gave their own daughters to their sons, and they served their gods. ⁷ The Israelites did evil in the LORD's sight; they forgot the LORD their God and served the Baals and the Asherahs. ⁸ The LORD's anger burned against Israel, and he sold them into the hand of Cushan-rishathaim king of Mesopotamia. The Israelites were subject to him for eight years. ⁹ When they cried out to the LORD, he raised up a deliverer for them: Othniel son of Kenaz, Caleb's younger brother. ¹⁰ The Spirit of the LORD came on him, and he led Israel. When he went out to war, the LORD gave Cushan-rishathaim king of Mesopotamia into his hands, and Othniel overpowered him.

¹¹ The land had peace for forty years, until Othniel son of Kenaz died. ¹² The Israelites again did evil in the LORD's sight, and because of this the LORD gave Eglon king of Moab power over them. ¹³ Eglon gathered the Ammonites and the Amalekites, attacked Israel, and captured the City of Palms. ¹⁴ The Israelites were subject to Eglon king of Moab for eighteen years. ¹⁵ Again they cried out to the LORD, and he raised up a deliverer for them: Ehud son of Gera the Benjaminite, a left-handed man. The Israelites sent tribute to Eglon king of Moab through Ehud.

¹⁶ Ehud had made himself a double-edged sword about eighteen inches long, which he strapped to his right thigh under his clothing. ¹⁷ He brought the tribute to Eglon king of Moab, who was a very fat man. ¹⁸ After Ehud had finished presenting the tribute, he sent off the men who had carried it. ¹⁹ But he himself turned back at the carved stones near Gilgal and said, "Your Majesty, I have a secret message for you." The king said, "Silence!" and all his attendants left. ²⁰ Ehud came to him while he was sitting alone in his cool upper room and said, "I have a message from God for you." As the king rose from his seat,

²¹ Ehud reached with his left hand, drew the sword from his right thigh, and plunged it into the king's belly. ²² The handle sank in after the blade, and the fat closed over it — he could not pull the sword out of his belly, and the contents of his bowels spilled out. ²³ Then Ehud went out through the porch, shut the doors of the upper room behind him, and locked them. ²⁴ After he had gone, the servants came back and found the doors of the upper room locked. They said, "He must be relieving himself in the cool inner room." ²⁵ They waited until they were embarrassed, but when he still did not open the doors, they took a key and unlocked them — and there was their master, fallen dead on the floor.

²⁶ While they were waiting, Ehud escaped; he slipped past the carved stones and made it safely to Seirah. ²⁷ When he arrived, he blew a trumpet in the hill country of Ephraim, and the Israelites came down from the hills with him at their head. ²⁸ He told them, "Follow me! The LORD has given your enemies the Moabites into your hands." So they followed him down, seized the fords of the Jordan ahead of the Moabites, and allowed no one to cross. ²⁹ At that time they struck down about ten thousand Moabites — all vigorous, strong men; not one escaped. ³⁰ That day Moab was subdued under Israel's hand, and the land had peace for eighty years.
³¹ After Ehud came Shamgar son of Anath, who struck down six hundred Philistines with an oxgoad. He too saved Israel.
